A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and v1's SG-DPS can be matched to v2's renamed SGDD despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic distributions, MNIST inverse problems, music infilling, and DNA generation, together with ablation and runtime results.

after.justification: v2 retains and extends these original experiments and adds FFHQ super-resolution and class-conditioned MNIST results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The Hamming-distance potential, alternating Metropolis-Hastings likelihood and discrete-diffusion prior steps, and geometric annealing remain unchanged. SG-DPS becomes SGDD with revised notation. The FFHQ experiment applies the same sampler in a discrete latent space; replacing Metropolis-Hastings with Langevin dynamics is explicitly left as future work.

E1.justification: v2 adds 4x super-resolution on FFHQ 256 and class-conditioned MNIST generation targeting digit 0 (Appendix D.1–D.2). Music infilling expands from 60% masked notes to both 40% and 60%. The original synthetic, DNA, MNIST inverse-problem, and music coverage remains.

E2.justification: SMC is added to the synthetic, MNIST XOR/AND, music, DNA, and runtime comparisons. The DNA comparison changes from SVDD-PM and DPS in v1 Table 4 to SVDD-PM, SMC, CG, TDS, and DRAKES with and without KL regularization in v2 Table 3; DPS is removed from that comparison.

E3.justification: DNA evaluation changes from 100 samples using an Enformer reward and alpha=0.1 to 640 samples with separate guidance and evaluation oracles, reported beta values of 30 and 50, and additional ATAC-accuracy and ELBO-based log-likelihood metrics. Its reported vocabulary changes from five to four symbols. New protocols include 100-image FFHQ evaluation using PSNR/LPIPS and class-conditioned MNIST evaluation using MSID and a separate classifier.

E4.justification: v2 adds a DNA guidance-strength sensitivity study over beta=3–100 that examines reward versus prior consistency (Figure 2), plus a quantitative class-conditioned posterior-fidelity analysis (Appendix D.2). The original annealing, computational-budget, and sampling-without-prior analyses are retained and relocated to Appendix B.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D.2 newly states that the evaluation classifier is trained with a different random seed. This adds seed information for an evaluation control, without establishing additional repeated sampler runs. Both versions otherwise retain per-sample mean and standard-deviation reporting without adding confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained synthetic and MNIST XOR/AND scores are unchanged, but v2 adds baseline and task results and replaces the DNA results under revised settings. At 60% music masking, reported SVDD-PM Hellinger distance/outlier means change from 0.503/0.242 to 0.529/0.114, while the proposed method retains 0.244/0.060. New results include SGDD's FFHQ PSNR of 25.85 and class-conditioned MNIST MSID of 14.59 (Tables 8–9).

T1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.5's fixed-noise average Fisher-divergence bound with score and discretization errors, assumptions and proofs in Appendix A, and spectral-gap/logarithmic-Sobolev reasoning in Appendix B.1. It also corrects the KL orientation in the SVDD variational objective (v1 Equation 30; v2 Equation 51). These are substantial formal changes, although the new proof contains an invalid inequality in Equation 31.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit theoretical contribution claiming convergence guarantees that account for score approximation and discretization errors. The DNA headline changes from 36% higher mean reward over SVDD-PM to 42% higher median activity over the strongest previous baseline, DRAKES without KL regularization, under the revised evaluation. The core plug-and-play sampling purpose and MNIST/music superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the DNA reward–likelihood tradeoff and a mixing-rate explanation for annealing. Appendix E.1 newly discusses restriction to uniform transition kernels, uncertain applicability to masked diffusion, and expensive forward-model evaluations during Metropolis-Hastings. Appendix D.1 distinguishes Euclidean-embedded latent codes from unordered categorical data and discusses possible acceleration.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, SMC implementation details, disclosure of three Monte Carlo samples for SVDD, and NVIDIA A100 runtime hardware. Conversely, v1's explicit Metropolis-Hastings initialization, token-flip proposal and acceptance equations, and likelihood-noise scales of 0.1 generally and 1 for synthetic data disappear. The documented 90M-parameter SEDD architecture and optimizer settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands theoretical positioning through finite-state Fisher-information, FIR-inequality, and Markov-chain literature, including Bobkov–Tetali and Hilder and colleagues. It also adds research supporting SMC comparisons, DRAKES, and latent-image experiments. The Enformer reference disappears with the DNA revision. These changes extend the paper's scientific positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: DNA experiments precede images and music, most ablation discussion moves to Appendix B, and experimental details become Appendix C alongside new theory, results, and discussion appendices. Method and setup passages are rewritten or compressed, notation changes throughout, and SG-DPS is renamed SGDD.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one. v2 adds a task-summary table, DNA tradeoff figure, and FFHQ/class-conditioned result tables, while expanding DNA and music table structures. Existing synthetic heatmaps, XOR sample grids, and ablation figures move to appendices. The MNIST diversity histogram remains present despite its shortened caption.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical assessment through separate DNA guidance/evaluation oracles, broader baselines, additional validation metrics, and explicit limitations. However, its central new convergence proof uses the false bound (1+u)ln(1+u) <= |u| in Equation 31: at u=0.5, the left side is approximately 0.608. Theorem 1 also concerns fixed-noise averaged divergence with residual errors, limiting what it establishes about exact posterior convergence. This unresolved theoretical support, together with removed sampling details, prevents a confident net quality judgment.
